title: Kernel pair of a quotient by a monomorphic equivalence relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U$ and $R$ be schemes over $S$, and let $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be a monomorphism whose image on $T$-points is an equivalence relation on $U(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$. Let $U/R$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site] of the presheaf quotient. Then the canonical map of fppf sheaves $h_R\to h_U\times_{U/R}h_U$ induced by $(s,t)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 045Y (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence), together with Definition of quotient sheaf immediately above it and the monomorphism hypothesis.

proof.text: Put $P(T)=U(T)/j(R(T))$ and $Q=P^\#=U/R$. The assumption that $j(R(T))$ is already an equivalence relation means that $[a]=[b]$ in $P(T)$ if and only if there is $r\in R(T)$ with $sr=a$ and $tr=b$; no chain of generated relations is needed. For a section $(a,b)$ of $h_U\times_Qh_U$ over $T$, the classes $[a],[b]\in P(T)$ have equal images in $Q(T)$. Apply the final assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] to $P$ on the big fppf site (with set values in a universe containing its objects and arrows). It gives an fppf covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ on which $[a|_{T_i}]=[b|_{T_i}]$. By the defining equivalence relation there are $r_i\in R(T_i)$ with $sr_i=a|_{T_i}$ and $tr_i=b|_{T_i}$. Hence the canonical map is locally surjective. Conversely any such relation sections give equality in $Q$ locally, and then globally by the separatedness of $Q$. This proves the local-witness assertion of Tag 045Y rather than assuming its omitted proof.

source.place: Tag 045Y (lemma-quotient-pre-equivalence), whose proof is omitted; its hint is completed using Sites Tags 00WB (theorem-plus) and 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification) via the cited existing local-sections lemma

proof.text: The same canonical morphism is locally injective. Suppose two sections r,r' of h_R over an S-scheme T have equal images in h_U x_Q h_U. After restricting to any member of a covering on which the equality is witnessed, their composites with s and t are equal. Thus j r=(s r,t r) and j r'=(s r',t r') are equal as maps to U x_S U. Since j is a monomorphism, r=r' on that member. This is exactly the local-injectivity condition for a morphism of sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 045Y, monomorphism hypothesis together with the definition of a monomorphism of schemes

proof.text: Apply the sheaf local-bijection criterion [lem-galois-set-sheaf-local-bijection-isomorphism] to the canonical map. Step 1 supplies local surjectivity and Step 2 supplies local injectivity, so the criterion gives that h_R -> h_U x_Q h_U is an isomorphism.
